chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Fletcher Henderson and the aloofness of big stars
summary: He loved Fletcher Henderson but explains how great bandleaders were hard to approach, with sidemen like Sonny Greer as gatekeepers.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well now, during that period, how did Fletcher Hendersom come off in person?

Oh, I loved him! Fletcher Henderson? We've got to be careful, these people are big people. The Jewish people are very big people. Just like a four-star general coming on the scene and you're a little corporal back there. What are you doing?

Now, Sonny Greer was the one who'd get you. "Cut it. Jack. a little) Sonny Greer was the one, you know, everybody was around Duke, "Oh, Mr. Ellington." "Oh, Mr. Fletcher Henderson." You'd be back there and it was hard to get to him. And if he wanted to stop, he wouldn't have time. Because these people are big. And even if he does know you, it's hard to get near him.
